subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 03, 2026
body:
The geocode‑glib update conflict that was blocking AcreetionOS‑Xlibre builds has been resolved, restoring GIS utilities for every Xlibre user. Natalie and Darren’s CI pipeline now ships a fully functional firefox‑ublock‑origin package alongside the fixed geocode‑glib integration, and the changelog already lists the fix under the September 3 2026 release. If you were stuck trying to use coordinate lookups in your Xlibre desktop, head over to the homepage https://acreetionos.org/ and grab the new ISO from the flash page to get the latest build.

Development
Natalie’s recent intelligence sync updated the newsletter archive and wiki guides, making it easier for new contributors to find documentation. The commit “Merge branch ‘main’ into release‑1: fix geocode‑glib update conflict in AcreetionOS‑Xlibre” cleaned up the dependency mess and also added the missing firefox‑ublock‑origin package, so privacy‑focused browsing works out of the box. You can read the full details on the changelog https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html or dive into the wiki for step‑by‑step setup.

Community
Incus 7.4 has officially dropped, bringing improved container and VM management to the ecosystem. The community hub announced the release on discuss.linuxcontainers.org, and many AcreetionOS users are already testing the new version on their hosts. The wiki page for Incus integration has been updated, so check it out via https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html if you want to upgrade.

Tip of the day
When you flash the latest AcreetionOS ISO to a USB drive, keep the “persistent” option enabled; this preserves your Firefox‑Ublock‑Origin settings and any custom geocode configurations across reboots, saving you a few clicks each session. Happy hacking!
